damage.en: His trousers were torn to shreds, his arm was damaged, and his eardrum burst.
damage.zh: 他的裤子被炸成了碎片，手臂受伤，耳膜破裂。

damage.en: The Remain Campaign warned that leaving would damage the economy and weaken Britain’s global influence.
damage.zh: “留欧派”阵营则警告称，离开将损害经济并削弱英国的全球影响力。

damage.en: Wear and tear refers to the damage that comes from using something every day.
damage.zh: “Wear and tear”指日常使用所带来的损伤。

damage.en: The shocks, the experimenter explained, could be painful, but they would cause no permanent damage.
damage.zh: 主试者解释说，这些电击可能会带来痛感，但不会造成永久性伤害。

damage.en: Both of these things can happen after particularly heavy rain and can cause damage to buildings.
damage.zh: 这两者都可能在暴雨之后发生，并对建筑物造成破坏。

damp.en: A good example of a word which does this is musty – a damp, stale smell you might find in an old bookshop.
damp.zh: 一个很好的例子就是 musty(霉味的)——指的是那种在旧书店里可能会闻到的潮湿、陈腐的气味。

damp.en: Listen as BBC presenters Marnie Chesterton and Tristan Ahtone describe the smells which give them the feeling of home: …My grandad's house smelt of pine and damp and musty books.
damp.zh: 听听BBC主持人Marnie Chesterton和Tristan Ahtone描述带给他们归属感的气味：……我爷爷的房子里有松树、潮湿和发霉的书籍的气味。

damp.en: But if we are chronically stressed - money worries, or a stressful job, or something that's going on forever, or life, or chronic sleep deprivation that's causing that level of stress, then you might constantly have a damped down immune system which can then lead to all these knock-on problems.
damp.zh: 但如果我们长期处于压力之中——比如金钱焦虑、压力大的工作、某种没完没了的事情、生活，或者导致这种压力水平的长期睡眠剥夺，那么你的免疫系统可能会一直处于低迷状态，进而导致所有这些连锁问题。

datum.en: Observational data is information collected from watching people's natural behaviour without interfering in it.
datum.zh: “Observational data”（观察性数据）是指在不进行干预的情况下，通过观察人们的自然行为收集的信息。

datum.en: And the computers in the data centre, of course, also need energy; they need electricity.
datum.zh: 当然，数据中心里的计算机也需要能量；它们需要电力。

datum.en: So that’s the data side. But it’s not just a question of numbers.
datum.zh: 这是数据的一面。但这并不只是数字的问题。

datum.en: The biggest of these is privacy. One major concern is how personal data is handled.
datum.zh: 其中最大的一个是隐私。一个主要的担忧是个人数据如何被处理。

datum.en: But we can't turn our noses up at the current data – the observational data.
datum.zh: 但我们不能对现有的数据——即观察性数据——嗤之以鼻。

dairy.en: It is the Netherlands. The UK imports £7.6 billion worth of imports, especially vegetables and dairy.
dairy.zh: 就是荷兰。英国从那里进口了价值 76 亿英镑的商品，尤其是蔬菜和乳制品。

dairy.en: People would also potentially have dairy products from cows and sheep, and perhaps keep chickens or other animals.
dairy.zh: 人们还可能拥有来自牛羊的乳制品，或许还会养鸡或其他动物。

dairy.en: Moving towards a sustainable food supply involves reducing the amount of meat and dairy we eat in favour of non-animal protein such as beans and lentils.
dairy.zh: 走向可持续的食物供应意味着减少我们食用的肉类和乳制品，转而食用非动物蛋白，如豆类和小扁豆。

dash.en: Into this era stepped Percy Harrison Fawcett: a dashing, determined British explorer with an uncanny ability to survive conditions that killed lesser men in days.
dash.zh: 踏入这个时代的是 Percy Harrison Fawcett：一位风度翩翩、意志坚定的英国探险家，他有着不可思议的能力，能在那些让普通人几天内丧命的环境中生存下来。

dash.en: You mentioned MySpace as one of the earliest social media platforms, but the first electronic message was actually sent much earlier, in 1844, using a series of dots and dashes tapped out by hand on a telegraph wire.
dash.zh: 你提到 MySpace 是最早的社交媒体平台之一，但第一条电子信息实际上发送得要早得多，是在 1844 年，通过在电报线上手工敲出一系列点和划来发送的。

dawn.en: We'll put it. It's just nonsense. Co-sleeping has been around since the dawn of time.
dawn.zh: 我们把它放那。这简直是胡说八道。同床睡从人类诞生之初就存在了。

dawn.en: He kept a working farm at Windsor. He went out before dawn to check on his livestock.
dawn.zh: 他在温莎经营着一个农场。他天不亮就出去查看牲畜。

dawn.en: A man who woke up before dawn to check on his crops.
dawn.zh: 一个日出前就醒来查看庄稼的男人。

dawn.en: Missiles are launched at dawn. Borders are crossed at night and the world wakes up to another war that no one wanted.
dawn.zh: 导弹在黎明时分发射。边境在夜间被跨越，世界在又一场无人想要的战争中醒来。

dawn.en: Not everyone bought it. To some, especially the urban middle class and Coptic Christians, it smelled like a power grab dressed up as reform; to others, people who had grown weary of corruption and poverty, it offered hope of a new dawn.
dawn.zh: 并非所有人都买账。对一些人来说，尤其是城市中产阶级和科普特基督徒，这闻起来就像是一场伪装成改革的权力争夺；而对另一些人来说，那些对腐败和贫困感到厌倦的人，它提供了一个新黎明希望。

dare.en: And those who faced the consequences were those who dared to challenge most openly.
dare.zh: 而那些面临后果的人，正是那些敢于最公开挑战的人。

dare.en: And the consequences go far deeper than simply getting to enjoy a hotter, and dare I say, tastier meal.
dare.zh: 其带来的影响远远超出了仅仅享受一顿更热、而且我敢说更美味的饭菜。

dare.en: I'm like, how dare she? But it really just came down to her just saying, I don't want to live your life.
dare.zh: 我说，她怎么敢？但归根结底，她只是说“我不想过你的生活”。

dare.en: Protests were banned, political opponents were jailed, and the secret police kept a watchful eye on anyone who dared to whisper a complaint.
dare.zh: 抗议活动被禁止，政治对手被投入监狱，秘密警察则密切监视着任何胆敢低声抱怨的人。

dare.en: In 1977, she brought a private prosecution against a newspaper called Gay News for publishing a poem called "The Love That Dares to Speak Its Name."
dare.zh: 1977 年，她对一家名为《Gay News》的报纸提起了一起私人诉讼，起因是该报发表了一首名为《敢于说出名字的爱》的诗。

damn.en: Or, as Goebbels neatly put it, “You have been in a damn hurry to get your witnesses below ground."
damn.zh: 或者，正如戈培尔精辟地说的那样：“你们可真够着急把证人送进地底下的。”

damn.en: Whether that is a damning contradiction or simply the reality of how American politics is funded, well, that’s something you can make up your own mind about.
damn.zh: 不管这算是一个致命的矛盾，还是仅仅体现了美国政治资金来源的现实，好吧，你可以自己下定论。

damn.en: Businessmen who had once been happy to be photographed beside him declined meetings, investors pulled out of the country, and newspaper columns were filled with damning reports.
damn.zh: 曾经乐于与他合影的商人们拒绝了会面，投资者撤出了该国，报纸专栏里充斥着 damning 的（罪证确凿的）报道。

damn.en: Fuck yeah. Yeah, damn right I do.
damn.zh: 去他的，没错，我确实这么想。

damn.en: Just by his footsteps, I knew. By the way he would close or open a door, I would know whether to be on edge or not. and so when i got that call everything in me let go like it was it was one of the most still is sort of like a painful memory you know is is like the first thought i had was damn it it happened i thought it would but not like this but it it it happened it happened yeah what is the cost you know because you described that spotty sense it almost sounds like a gift and the interesting thing to some degree it can be a gift yeah it is a gift i think every gift is a curse and i think every curse is a gift and what is the curse that comes with the gift so the curse that comes with it is i exist in a space where i am too aware of how other people feel you know and and as i've come to understand it what happens to a lot of children who are in abusive households is they develop their hypersensitivity as a tool to protect the parent because they start in the same way you were saying with your dad, why is he just sitting here?
damn.zh: 仅仅通过他的脚步声，我就知道。通过他关门或开门的方式，我就知道是否要保持警惕。所以当我接到那个电话时，我内心的一切都崩溃了，就像它仍然是一种痛苦的记忆，你知道，第一个念头是：该死，它发生了。我以为会发生，但不是这样，但它发生了，它发生了。是的，代价是什么？因为你描述的那种蜘蛛感应听起来几乎是一种天赋，有趣的是，在某种程度上它确实可以是天赋。是的，它是一种天赋，我认为每种天赋都是一种诅咒，我认为每种诅咒都是一种天赋。那么伴随天赋而来的诅咒是什么？伴随它而来的诅咒是我存在于一个空间里，我对别人的感受太敏感了，你知道，正如我所理解的那样，很多处于虐待家庭的孩子会发展出这种高度敏感作为保护父母的工具，因为他们开始以你和你父亲的方式，为什么他只是坐在那里？

daring.en: In Britain, to most he is a romantic figure, a daring adventurer.
daring.zh: 在英国，对大多数人来说，他是一个浪漫的人物，一个大胆的冒险家。

daring.en: And I was daring myself to do it. And I did it.
daring.zh: 我当时是在给自己壮胆。然后我照做了。

daring.en: A seasoned Roman commander, Publius Cornelius Scipio, fresh from victories in Iberia, led a daring campaign in North Africa.
daring.zh: 一位经验丰富的罗马统帅——刚在伊比利亚取得胜利的普布利乌斯·科尔内利乌斯·西庇阿（Publius Cornelius Scipio），在北非发起了一场大胆的远征。

daring.en: Today, Percy Fawcett is often called “the real-life Indiana Jones,” a moniker that suits his larger-than-life persona and daring exploits.
daring.zh: 如今，Percy Fawcett 常被称为“现实版的 Indiana Jones”，这个绰号非常符合他传奇般的人物性格和惊险刺激的壮举。
